newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN TENNIS PLAYER SEES 1997 GOOD YEAR.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN TENNIS PLAYER SEES 1997 GOOD YEAR.

text.p: Belgian's smiling and chatty tennis heroine Sabine Appelmans returned to Belgium from the Australian Open on Thursday convinced she could power past any of the top-seeded players in future matches.
"I think I can beat anyone," world number 18 Appelmans, who lost against French Mary Pierce in a close Australian Open quarter-finals, told a press conference at Brussels airport.
Appelmans and compatriot Dominique van Roost-Monami, ranked 43, both reached the quarter-finals, the first time Belgium has advanced so far in any grand slam tournament.
She said her goal this year was to improve her ranking and near the 10 top players.
Asked what went wrong in the quarter-finals she said she had been nervous before the match and that "I only thought of beating (Mary) Pierce, not on how I was playing, this I have to improve".
"The most important thing I've learnt is to stay calm in every match," she told Reuters.
"Next time I'm at centre court I'll be better prepared for it".
She said the temperature which soared to almost 50 degrees during the tournament was the hardest battle she faced there.
Appelmans will play next in Linz, Austria.
